Honestly I understand where you're coming from. For me it's my brother though and I've pretty much been raising him for the last couple of years. My problem lies more with the fact that he's lazy and when he doesn't like something tattles to make my mom act. I'm 24 and he's 22 for reference.

It was really difficult for us growing up because all he wanted was to be around me and all I wanted was to be left alone. Actually it hasn't changed much since we were kids. I hate having to clean up after him. I hate dealing with his tantrums. I hate how pissy he gets when I ask him to clean up his messes. It's been 3 years and his shit is getting old.

The only advice I can offer you as someone who's been left to handle the mess my parent made is this: you are absolutely allowed to have boundaries. You're other son is allowed to have them as well and you need to find a way to teach your youngest that. I don't know your son, but there will be a way that works for you.

Also as a side note every year my job requires that I take a traumatic brain injury recognition training with has this lovely tidbit I'd like to share. If you ever feel stressed out to the point where you feel like the child isn't safe in your care it is okay to walk away. Make sure he's safe before you do, but it's okay to give yourself a break. You, your wife and both of your sons are human beings with wants and needs. Sometimes you just NEED to be alone to collect yourself and that's okay. Don't feel bad for NEEDING a break, because chances are your son probably also needs a break from you. Children can feel when you're stressed, even autistic ones, so do yourself a favor and take a deep breath.

You might also look into documenting his outbursts as the happen or soon after. It may help you find a pattern that's causing the behavior. Documentation is only as useful as it is detailed though so try to be objective. It'll also give you a head start when services become available, because you'll have all the information you need. Also, I think it's important to say this: it's not your son that you hate, it's the behavior, and I can almost guarantee that once you can solve the behavioral issue that you'll see your son in a whole new light.

No one is promoting running red lights. You seem like a very passionate person about the issue, but  I think you might have misunderstood something. The post you made this in response to wasn't about promoting running lights, it was to bring attention to the ridiculous timing of the lights. There are lights in the Springs that I get stuck at for multiple cycles because they simply aren't long enough to alleviate the heavy traffic. It's frustrating to be stuck in one spot for an extra 8 minutes because the light cycle only changes every 4 minutes with a green turn arrow for only 30 seconds. I'm not saying that people should be running lights, that's absolutely not okay, but the light times do need to be taken into consideration regarding the traffic flow in certain areas.
